context: A uni student gives his teen friend advice about high school clubs
purpose: Teach: 教養/キャンパス/スペシャル/部会/講習/グランド/早朝/史上

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: 先輩、高校って部活どれ選べばいいか全然わかんないんですけど。
lines.en: Senpai, I have no idea which club to pick in high school.
lines.style: Teenage girl sounding lost and seeking guidance from an older mentor

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 迷うよな。俺の大学のキャンパスでも同じ話よく聞くよ。
lines.en: It's tough. Even on my university campus I hear that all the time.
lines.style: University guy speaking warmly and casually like an older brother

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: 運動部だとグランドで早朝練習があるって聞いて、ちょっと怖いんです。
lines.en: I heard sports clubs do early morning practice on the field, which scares me a bit.
lines.style: Teenage girl voicing nervous hesitation with a slightly whiny tone

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 確かにきついけど、史上最強の青春になるって先輩たちは言ってたな。
lines.en: It's rough, sure, but the seniors used to say it makes for the greatest youth ever.
lines.style: University guy reminiscing fondly with a nostalgic, encouraging warmth

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: 文化部はどうですかね?教養が身につくって母は言うんですけど。
lines.en: What about cultural clubs? My mom says they build real refinement and knowledge.
lines.style: Teenage girl quoting her mother with mild skepticism and curiosity

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: いいと思うよ。文化系の部会に入れば、夏休みの講習とかも充実してるし。
lines.en: I think that's great. Joining a cultural club committee means solid summer workshops too.
lines.style: University guy giving thoughtful, supportive advice in a relaxed tone

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: あ、文化祭のスペシャルステージとかも出られるんですよね?
lines.en: Oh, and you can perform on the special stage at the school festival too, right?
lines.style: Teenage girl suddenly perking up with excited, hopeful realization

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: そうそう。とりあえず体験入部してみなよ。合わなきゃ変えればいいんだから。
lines.en: Exactly. Just go try them out first—if it doesn't fit, you can switch.
lines.style: University guy wrapping up with relaxed, reassuring big-brother energy
